thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert — realtime inference p99 > 2.5s (streaming) across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Auto-page to #eng-oncall and #incidents :rotating_light:
Maria: Paging Jack (oncall) — looks like p99 spike started ~5m ago, p95 up a bit too. Can you take? :phone:
Jack: Ack. I'm awake, looking now. First check: dashboards + recent deploys.
Lee: I see the spike correlates with a deploy 7m ago from `release/runtime/2.14.0` (canary rolled). Deploy-bot shows canary finished at +6m.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment `release/runtime/2.14.0` completed on eu-west-1. No immediate errors reported.
Jack: Copy. Pulling up traces, heatmap and live tail.
Sam: Quick note — streaming endpoints show a pattern: many sessions stuck in TEARDOWN state but still holding kernels. Might be streaming chunk flush changes.
Maria: Customer impact: a few high-throughput customers reported slow chat responses (visible in support queue). No broad 5xxs though.
Alex: Running a quick datadog query: `avg(last_5m):p99(stream.latency){env:prod,endpoint:stream} by {region,model}` — returns p99 ~ 2.9s eu-west-1, 2.6s us-west-2, other regions fine.
Jack: Traces show long tail inside `runtime/stream_muxer` during first chunk flush. Stack looks like backpressure in async write path.
Maria: Any CPU/GPU saturation?
Lee: GPU util looks normal. CPU on control-plane pods spiked on canary nodes around the same time (sys CPU up ~45% -> 80%).
Jack: That matches — runtime change in 2.14.0 introduced extra sync on chunk flush (suspect).
Sam: Can we quickly rollback the runtime canary? If it's the culprit we need immediate mitigation.
Jack: I'm going to pause routing to canary nodes and shift traffic to stable pool. Executing routing command now.
Jack: `rtctl route set-policy --service=streaming --exclude-pool=runtime-2.14-canary`
Maria: :thumbsup: Notify customers? Ops can post in status if we need to escalate.
deploy-bot: Routing update applied: 12% of traffic removed from runtime-2.14-canary.
Alex: After 60s, p99 in eu-west-1 dropped from 2.9s -> 1.4s. us-west-2 trending down as well.
Jack: Great — looks like routing fix helped. I'll continue with a full rollback of the canary.
Lee: Recommend also enabling model-fallback to 8-bit quantized variant for heavy customers for a few minutes to reduce kernel pressure.
Sam: Doing a selective fallback for two flagged customers (customer-a, customer-b) now.
Sam: `apictl set-model-override --customer customer-a --model model-x-q8`
Maria: Customer-a support thread updated, letting them know we're investigating and retrying requests will help for now.
Jack: Rolling runtime canary back to stable across eu-west-1. `deploy rollback runtime 2.14.0 --region eu-west-1 --canary`
deploy-bot: Rollback started. ETA ~2m.
Jack: Observability checklist: confirm p99 by region, confirm no error rate increase, confirm no new OOMs, note deploy id.
Alex: After rollback complete, p99 eu-west-1 is at 1.1s. Streaming stalls count fell to baseline.
Maria: Triage notes: probable root cause = introduced sync in streaming chunk flush path in runtime v2.14.0 => increased control-plane CPU causing extra head-of-line latency for streaming sessions.
Lee: Action items: 1) Revert code path in runtime and run targeted unit & integration tests for streaming chunking. 2) Add a canary throttling rule to limit control-plane CPU uptake during canary. 3) Add an alert for sudden increase in control-plane CPU on canary nodes.
Jack: I'll open a postmortem ticket and assign owners. For now we're in mitigation/monitoring mode. Paging cleared but leaving thread open for post-rollback checks.
Maria: Thanks all. Marking high-priority follow-up and notifying support & customer success to reach out to impacted customers.
Alex: Quick query I'll attach to postmortem: `topk(5, p99(stream.latency) by model) over last 10m` — shows model-x as top offender during window.
Sam: Noted. Will capture logs from the canary nodes and attach debug dump.
Jack: Final check: error budget burn for streaming SLO briefly exceeded p99 threshold, recording incident for SLO dashboard.
Maria: Closing on-call handoff: Jack -> Lee for follow-ups. Jack, ping if anything re-opens.
Jack: Copy. Leaving the channel but subscribed to updates.
incident-bot: Incident: SEV2 -> Mitigated (routing rollback applied). Incident created: INC-2026-4932. Postmortem required.
Maria: Thanks team :heart:
